rules.whatItMeans: A CI has had no update of any kind — no discovery, no integration, no manual edit — since it was created.
rules.whyItMatters: Either it is inert and should be retired, or it is real and nothing is watching it. Both need resolution.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci.sys_created_on vs sys_updated_on
rules.detectionLogic: CIs where sys_updated_on equals sys_created_on (within tolerance) AND age exceeds threshold
rules.threshold: Age threshold default 180 days
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on timestamp comparison.
rules.evidenceToShow: CI list with age, creating source, class, and any task references.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Genuinely static reference CIs.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 — retire or bring under discovery

rules.title: Source last-seen age per attribute
rules.whatItMeans: The age of the last report from each source, measured per attribute rather than per record.
rules.whyItMatters: A CI can look fresh because one source updates one field daily while every other attribute is two years old. Record-level freshness hides this completely.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_metadata / last-seen data per attribute per source
rules.detectionLogic: Per attribute per class: age of the most recent source report
rules.threshold: Per-attribute thresholds; identity attributes tighter than descriptive
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on timestamp data where the metadata table is populated.
rules.evidenceToShow: Attribute-level freshness heatmap by class, contrasted with record-level freshness.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Attribute metadata not maintained on this instance. The rule cannot fire without it; report that as a gap instead.
rules.crossDomainLink: Exposes freshness that record-level metrics overstate

rules.title: CI updated only by scripts for N months
rules.whatItMeans: A CI has been updated only by scripts or integrations, never by discovery or a human, for an extended period.
rules.whyItMatters: The CI is being maintained by something that may not have authoritative knowledge. Often an integration keeping a record alive that discovery no longer sees.
rules.sourceTables: sys_audit updated_by analysis, discovery evidence
rules.detectionLogic: CIs where all updates in the window are from script or integration users AND no discovery confirmation exists
rules.threshold: Window default 180 days
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — depends on correct classification of updating users.
rules.evidenceToShow: CI list, the updating process, what it updates, and the absence of discovery confirmation.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimate integration-managed CI classes (cloud resources, SaaS).
rules.crossDomainLink: Suggests discovery gap masked by integration activity

rules.title: Percentage sourced only from manual create
rules.whatItMeans: The percentage of CIs whose only provenance is a manual create.
rules.whyItMatters: Manually created CIs are never automatically corrected. They drift from reality from the moment they are entered, and nothing detects it.
rules.sourceTables: Creation source attribution
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(CIs created manually with no subsequent source confirmation) / total
rules.threshold: Default threshold 25%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ratio by class, creating users, creation date distribution, and age.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Classes where manual entry is the only possible source.

rules.title: Percentage sourced only from import set
rules.whatItMeans: The percentage of CIs whose only provenance is an import set.
rules.whyItMatters: Import-created CIs inherit the quality of the source file and are rarely re-validated. Often a one-time migration population nobody has revisited.
rules.sourceTables: Creation source attribution, sys_import_set linkage
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(CIs created by import with no subsequent source confirmation) / total
rules.threshold: Default threshold 25%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ratio by class, the import sets responsible, their dates, and whether the import still runs.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Ongoing import from an authoritative external system.
rules.crossDomainLink: Often the population behind Group 2 and 3 defects

rules.title: Retired CI still holding active relationships
rules.whatItMeans: A CI is marked retired but still holds active relationships.
rules.whyItMatters: Traversal includes decommissioned infrastructure in live results. Impact analysis returns a confident wrong answer that includes things that no longer exist.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci lifecycle fields, cmdb_rel_ci
rules.detectionLogic: CIs in a retired state with one or more active edges
rules.threshold: Retired state set read from instance configuration
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on state and edge check.
rules.evidenceToShow: CI, its state, its edges, the connected CIs and their states, and the retirement date.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Retirement in progress with a documented decommission change open.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 1 — retire the edges, snapshot held

rules.title: Retired CI still on an active service map
rules.whatItMeans: A retired CI still appears on an active service map.
rules.whyItMatters: The service map asserts dependency on something decommissioned. Every impact calculation using that map is wrong, and service mapping will not self-correct because the CI is no longer discovered.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci lifecycle, svc_ci_assoc, service map data
rules.detectionLogic: Retired-state CIs present in an active service map association
rules.threshold: Active map definition configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on state and association check.
rules.evidenceToShow: CI, state, the maps including it, the services affected, and the map's last refresh date.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Map not refreshed since a legitimate recent retirement. Check retirement date against map refresh.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 1 — remove from map, trigger remap

rules.title: Decommissioned in asset but active in CMDB
rules.whatItMeans: The asset record shows the item decommissioned or disposed while the CI shows it active, or the reverse.
rules.whyItMatters: Asset and CMDB disagree on whether the thing exists. Finance, audit and operations each read a different system and get a different answer.
rules.sourceTables: alm_asset / alm_hardware state, cmdb_ci lifecycle, asset-CI link
rules.detectionLogic: Linked asset-CI pairs where lifecycle states are contradictory
rules.threshold: State mapping between asset and CI lifecycle models, configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — depends on the correctness of the state mapping.
rules.evidenceToShow: Both records, both states, the link, the last update on each, and the source of each update.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimate lag during a decommission workflow. Check for an open decommission task.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 — which record is right is an asset-management judgement
rules.crossDomainLink: Asset reconciliation; feeds Data Quality model

rules.title: Deleted CI leaving orphaned relationships
rules.whatItMeans: A CI has been deleted but its relationships remain, pointing at a record that no longer exists.
rules.whyItMatters: Traversal encounters a broken reference. Depending on the consumer this either errors or silently drops the branch, truncating impact results without warning.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_rel_ci parent and child sys_ids vs cmdb_ci existence
rules.detectionLogic: Edges where either endpoint sys_id has no corresponding CI record
rules.threshold: Any occurrence
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% — the referenced record exists or it does not.
rules.evidenceToShow: Orphaned edge, the missing sys_id, the surviving endpoint, and the deletion event from audit if retained.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: None. This is always a defect.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 1 — delete the orphaned edge, snapshot held

rules.title: Retired CI referenced by open incidents or changes
rules.whatItMeans: A retired CI is still referenced by open incidents, changes or requests.
rules.whyItMatters: Work is being tracked against something that officially does not exist. Either the retirement was premature or the tasks were never reassigned.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci lifecycle, task tables referencing cmdb_ci
rules.detectionLogic: Retired-state CIs with one or more open task references
rules.threshold: Open state set per task table
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on reference check.
rules.evidenceToShow: CI, state, retirement date, the open tasks with their ages and assignment groups.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Tasks deliberately open to complete the decommission itself.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 — task reassignment is an operational decision
rules.crossDomainLink: ITSM linkage; often reveals incomplete decommission

rules.title: Retired CIs present in principal class
rules.whatItMeans: Retired CIs remain in principal classes and are therefore included in health scoring.
rules.whyItMatters: Drags scores down for a population that should be out of scope, and obscures the true health of the live estate. Distortion rather than operational failure, hence High not Critical on its own.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci lifecycle (install_status, life_cycle_stage/_status), cmdb_class_info.principal_class, cmdb_health_config (inclusion rules: applies_to, active_record_condition, metric → cmdb_health_metric; weights in cmdb_health_metric_pref).
rules.detectionLogic: Retired-state CIs within classes covered by health inclusion rules whose filters do not exclude retired states
rules.threshold: Depends on inclusion rule filter construction Fallback (v3): when no principal classes are designated (see CMDB-139), evaluate all populated CMDB classes and name the fallback in the finding.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on state and scope check.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by class, the inclusion rule filter, and the score with and without retired CIs.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deliberate inclusion to track retirement backlog. Report both scores.

rules.title: Lifecycle contradicting asset lifecycle
rules.whatItMeans: CI lifecycle state contradicts the lifecycle recorded on its linked asset.
rules.whyItMatters: The narrower, record-level version of CMDB-082, scoped to lifecycle fields specifically rather than overall state.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci lifecycle fields, alm_asset lifecycle fields, link
rules.detectionLogic: Linked pairs where lifecycle values map to different stages
rules.threshold: Mapping table between CI and asset lifecycle models
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — mapping-dependent.
rules.evidenceToShow: Both lifecycle values, the mapping, and the update history on each.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimate transitional lag.

rules.title: CIs in Absent or Stolen status still operational
rules.whatItMeans: CIs in Absent or Stolen install_status still show an operational operational_status.
rules.whyItMatters: The estate is recording that a device is missing and simultaneously that it is running. One of those is a security or loss-reporting matter, not just a data defect.
rules.sourceTables: install_status, operational_status
rules.detectionLogic: CIs with install_status in {Absent, Stolen} AND operational_status in an operational set
rules.threshold: State sets read from instance configuration
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on state check.
rules.evidenceToShow: CI list, both states, last_discovered, any recent task activity, and the assigned owner.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Status set in error rather than reflecting an actual loss. Verify before escalating to security.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 — may require a security or loss report, not a data fix

rules.title: Retirement backlog beyond N days
rules.whatItMeans: CIs flagged as stale beyond a threshold have had no retirement action taken.
rules.whyItMatters: Detection happened; action did not. The stale population grows and dilutes every other metric.
rules.sourceTables: Staleness flags or derived staleness, retirement task or state changes
rules.detectionLogic: CIs stale beyond threshold with no retirement task and no state change
rules.threshold: Default 180 days stale with no action
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on arithmetic.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by class, age distribution, and the owning groups.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Retirement deliberately deferred pending a project.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 then Lane 1 bulk state change

rules.title: No lifecycle change since creation
rules.whatItMeans: A CI's lifecycle state has never changed since creation despite significant age.
rules.whyItMatters: Suggests lifecycle is not being managed at all for that class. Weak individually, strong as a class-level ratio.
rules.sourceTables: sys_audit on lifecycle fields, CI age
rules.detectionLogic: CIs with no lifecycle field audit entry AND age above threshold
rules.threshold: Age threshold default 365 days. Report as a class ratio.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on audit absence. Report as a pattern, not per record.
rules.evidenceToShow: Percentage per class with no lifecycle change, and the age distribution.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Long-lived infrastructure legitimately in one state.

rules.title: Retired CIs not archived per retention policy
rules.whatItMeans: Retired CIs have not been archived or deleted in line with the defined retention policy.
rules.whyItMatters: Table growth and query cost. Lowest severity in the group; matters at scale and for data retention compliance.
rules.sourceTables: Retired CI counts and ages, archival rule configuration
rules.detectionLogic: Retired CIs older than the retention period with no archival record
rules.threshold: Retention period from policy configuration, not assumed
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% where policy is configured. Where no policy exists, this becomes CMDB-101.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by class and age, the configured retention period, and archival rule state.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: No retention policy defined — report CMDB-101 instead.
rules.crossDomainLink: Feeds Group 13 scale and DPDP retention

rules.title: Percentage of principal classes under active governance (below 50%)
rules.whatItMeans: The percentage of principal classes under active Data Manager governance — with a configured owner, attestation cycle and remediation policy.
rules.whyItMatters: Tells the customer, and their auditor, how much of the CMDB is actually governed as opposed to merely populated.
rules.sourceTables: Data Manager configuration, principal class list
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(principal classes with active governance config) / COUNT(principal classes)
rules.threshold: Default threshold 50% Fallback (v3): when no principal classes are designated (see CMDB-139), evaluate all populated CMDB classes and name the fallback in the finding.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration presence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Class list with governance state, owner, cycle and policy per class.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Governance managed outside ServiceNow with documented evidence.

rules.title: Attestation cycle never run despite being scheduled
rules.whatItMeans: An attestation cycle is configured and scheduled but has never executed.
rules.whyItMatters: The customer reports an active attestation programme that has produced zero attestations. This is an audit finding, not a data finding.
rules.sourceTables: Attestation configuration, execution history
rules.detectionLogic: Attestation configs with active=true AND zero execution records
rules.threshold: Fixed: zero executions
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on execution record absence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Config, schedule, creation date, and empty execution history.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Configured within the current cycle and not yet due.

rules.title: Attester is inactive user or empty group
rules.whatItMeans: The assigned attester is an inactive user, or a group with no active members.
rules.whyItMatters: Attestation can never complete. The control exists and cannot function, which is the most common shape of a failed control.
rules.sourceTables: Attestation assignment, sys_user.active, sys_user_grmember
rules.detectionLogic: Attestation configs whose attester resolves to an inactive user or a group with zero active members
rules.threshold: Active membership evaluated at run time, not from group record alone
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% — the attester resolves to someone active or does not.
rules.evidenceToShow: Config, the attester reference, the user or group state, and the pending attestations blocked by it.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: None.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 — reassignment is an ownership decision

rules.title: Attestation configured with no attester assigned
rules.whatItMeans: Attestation is configured for a class but no attester has been assigned at all.
rules.whyItMatters: Weaker than CMDB-093 because it is visibly incomplete rather than deceptively complete, but the effect is the same: nothing attests.
rules.sourceTables: Attestation configuration attester field
rules.detectionLogic: Attestation configs with an empty attester field
rules.threshold: Fixed: empty field
rules.evidenceToShow: Config list with empty attester, and the class and CI count each covers.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Config in draft.

rules.title: Attestation failed
rules.whatItMeans: Attestations have been executed and returned a failed result.
rules.whyItMatters: The control worked. Someone looked and said the data is wrong. These are the highest-quality findings in the entire CMDB model because a human has already validated them.
rules.sourceTables: Attestation results, failure reasons
rules.detectionLogic: Attestation records with a failed outcome in the window
rules.threshold: Report by class, attester and failure reason
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the result. The attester's judgement is the evidence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Failed attestations with reason, class, CI set, attester and date.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: None. Treat these as confirmed findings.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 1 or Lane 3 depending on the failure reason

rules.title: Archival/deletion rules missing on high-growth classes
rules.whatItMeans: High-growth CI classes have no archival or deletion rules configured.
rules.whyItMatters: Unbounded growth with no exit path. Query cost rises continuously and retention compliance has no mechanism.
rules.sourceTables: Class growth rates, archival rule configuration
rules.detectionLogic: Classes with growth above threshold AND no archival or deletion rule
rules.threshold: Growth threshold configurable, default top decile by growth rate
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration absence; growth ranking is computed.
rules.evidenceToShow: Class list with growth rate, current row count, and projected size, alongside archival config state.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Retention handled by an external archival process.

rules.title: Attestation overdue
rules.whatItMeans: Attestations are past their due date and not yet completed.
rules.whyItMatters: A workflow state, not a data defect. Matters as an adherence trend rather than an individual finding, hence Moderate.
rules.sourceTables: Attestation records with due dates
rules.detectionLogic: Attestations in a pending state past due date
rules.threshold: Report count and age distribution
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on date arithmetic.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count, age distribution, and distribution by attester.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimate extension granted.

rules.title: Attestation pending
rules.whatItMeans: Attestations are issued and awaiting response within their due window.
rules.whyItMatters: Not a defect at all. Included as a workload and pipeline measure. Deliberately Low, and worth saying so in front of a CMDB manager who has been shown dashboards that treat this as a problem.
rules.sourceTables: Attestation records in pending state
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(pending attestations within due window)
rules.threshold: Report as a measure, not a threshold
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on count.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count and distribution by attester and class.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: None — this is a measure.

rules.title: Data certification tasks ageing
rules.whatItMeans: Data certification tasks are open and ageing beyond threshold.
rules.whyItMatters: The certification workflow is not completing. Similar to CMDB-097 but for the task-based certification path.
rules.sourceTables: Data certification task table
rules.detectionLogic: Open certification tasks with age above threshold
rules.threshold: Default 60 days
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on age arithmetic.
rules.evidenceToShow: Task list with age, assignee, and the class or filter each covers.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Tasks parked pending a data source fix.

rules.title: De-dup task backlog
rules.whatItMeans: The backlog of open de-duplication tasks, as a governance measure rather than a per-task finding.
rules.whyItMatters: Complements CMDB-042 and CMDB-043. The backlog size relative to creation rate tells you whether the team is keeping up.
rules.sourceTables: De-duplication task table
rules.detectionLogic: Open task count, creation rate, closure rate, and the resulting net position
rules.threshold: Report all three numbers together
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on counts.
rules.evidenceToShow: Backlog size, creation vs closure rate chart, and projected backlog.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: None.

rules.title: Retention policy defined per class and adherence
rules.whatItMeans: Retention policy is not defined per class, or is defined and not adhered to.
rules.whyItMatters: Two findings in one rule. Absence of policy is a governance gap; non-adherence is a control failure. Both matter for DPDP where CI data includes personal references.
rules.sourceTables: Retention policy configuration per class, retired CI ages
rules.detectionLogic: Classes with no retention policy; plus classes with policy where retired CI age exceeds it
rules.threshold: Report the two cases separately
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration; 100% on age arithmetic where policy exists.
rules.evidenceToShow: Class list with policy state, retention period, and the count of CIs exceeding it.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Retention governed at the instance level rather than per class.

rules.title: Support group has zero active members
rules.whatItMeans: The support group assigned to a CI has zero active members.
rules.whyItMatters: The most valuable ownership finding in the set, because it exposes the metric itself as false. The dashboard reports ownership complete; at two in the morning there is nobody to call. Report nominal and effective ownership separately and show the gap.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci.support_group, sys_user_grmember, sys_user.active
rules.detectionLogic: CIs whose support group resolves to zero active members at evaluation time
rules.threshold: Active membership resolved live, not from the group record
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% — membership resolves to a person or it does not.
rules.evidenceToShow: CI count by group, the empty groups, their last membership change date, and the Business Critical services affected.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Group deliberately empty pending a transition, with a documented interim owner elsewhere.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 — reassignment is an ownership decision, then Lane 1 bulk apply
rules.crossDomainLink: Cross-links to Data Quality Q2; invalidates D9 nominal completeness

rules.title: Owner is an inactive user
rules.whatItMeans: The CI owner is an inactive user.
rules.whyItMatters: Notifications, approvals and escalations routed to this owner go nowhere. The field is populated, so every completeness metric counts it as a pass.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci.owned_by, managed_by, assigned_to; sys_user.active
rules.detectionLogic: CIs whose owner reference resolves to a user with active=false
rules.threshold: Evaluate all ownership fields in use on the class
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on user state.
rules.evidenceToShow: CI count by inactive owner, the owner's deactivation date, and the CIs' criticality.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: User deactivated within a grace period with a documented successor.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 1 where a successor is inferable from group or manager, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.title: Classes with no defined data owner
rules.whatItMeans: CI classes have no defined data owner at the class level — nobody is accountable for the quality of that class.
rules.whyItMatters: Without class ownership there is no path to remediation. Findings have no recipient, and every improvement effort stalls at the question of whose job it is.
rules.sourceTables: Data Manager class ownership configuration, principal class list
rules.detectionLogic: Principal classes with no class-level data owner configured
rules.threshold: Fixed: absence of configuration Fallback (v3): when no principal classes are designated (see CMDB-139), evaluate all populated CMDB classes and name the fallback in the finding.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration absence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Class list with CI counts, defect counts, and absence of owner, ranked by defect volume.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Ownership held in an external RACI with documented evidence.
rules.crossDomainLink: Blocks remediation of every other finding in that class

rules.title: CI with no owner, manager or support group
rules.whatItMeans: A CI has no owner, no managed_by and no support group — no accountability reference of any kind.
rules.whyItMatters: Nobody owns it. Incidents against it cannot route, changes cannot be approved by an owner, and no attestation can be assigned.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci ownership fields
rules.detectionLogic: CIs where all configured ownership fields are empty
rules.threshold: Field set per class
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on emptiness.
rules.evidenceToShow: CI count by class, with any inferable owner signal: incident assignment history, change approver history, parent service owner.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Classes where ownership is genuinely held at the service level rather than the CI level.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 1 where strongly inferable from history, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.title: Ownership inconsistent with parent application service
rules.whatItMeans: A CI's ownership differs from the ownership of the application service it supports.
rules.whyItMatters: Not automatically wrong, but it means escalation paths diverge. During an incident, two different groups believe they own the response, or neither does.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci ownership, application service ownership, svc_ci_assoc and cmdb_rel_ci
rules.detectionLogic: CIs whose owner or support group differs from that of their supporting application service
rules.threshold: Report as a ratio per service before raising individual findings
rules.confidenceBasis: 80% — divergence is a signal, not proof of error.
rules.evidenceToShow: The CI, the service, both ownership sets, and the incident routing history for each.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimate separation between infrastructure ownership and service ownership. Confirm the estate's convention.

rules.title: Single owner holding disproportionate share
rules.whatItMeans: A single user or group owns a disproportionate share of the CI estate.
rules.whyItMatters: Concentration risk. Usually indicates bulk assignment during migration rather than real ownership, and it creates a single point of failure in the accountability model.
rules.sourceTables: Ownership field distribution
rules.detectionLogic: Owners holding more than N percent of CIs in scope
rules.threshold: Default 20% of the in-scope estate. Report distribution regardless.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on distribution. The judgement that it is wrong is advisory.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ownership distribution chart, top owners with counts, and the assignment date pattern.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: A genuinely centralised infrastructure team.

rules.title: Ownership unchanged since creation
rules.whatItMeans: Ownership has never changed since CI creation despite organisational change.
rules.whyItMatters: Weak signal alone, meaningful as a class-level ratio. Suggests ownership was set once at migration and never maintained.
rules.sourceTables: sys_audit on ownership fields, CI age
rules.detectionLogic: CIs with no ownership field audit entry AND age above threshold
rules.threshold: Age threshold default 365 days. Report as ratio.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on audit absence. Report as a pattern.
rules.evidenceToShow: Percentage per class with no ownership change, and age distribution.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Stable ownership is legitimate and common.

rules.title: Business Service unreachable from any CI
rules.whatItMeans: A Business Service cannot be reached by graph traversal from any CI — there is no path upward from infrastructure to the service.
rules.whyItMatters: The service exists as a record and is disconnected from the estate. No infrastructure event can ever reach it, so it will never appear in an impact result no matter what fails.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_rel_ci adjacency, svc_ci_assoc, CSDM service classes
rules.detectionLogic: Business Services with no inbound traversal path from any CI within the depth limit
rules.threshold: Depth limit default 8; state it with the result
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on traversal absence at the stated depth.
rules.evidenceToShow: The service, its criticality, its incident volume, and the tier at which any partial path terminates.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Services deliberately modelled as business constructs with no infrastructure (a contractual service).
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 then Lane 1 — structure decision then bulk edge creation
rules.crossDomainLink: The CSDM-side view of CMDB-057; core of the router demo

rules.title: Application Service with no supporting CIs
rules.whatItMeans: An Application Service has no supporting CIs associated to it.
rules.whyItMatters: The service layer terminates with nothing beneath it. Service maps are empty, impact analysis stops here, and the CSDM chain is decorative rather than functional.
rules.sourceTables: Application Service records, svc_ci_assoc, cmdb_rel_ci
rules.detectionLogic: Application Services with zero CI associations and zero supporting edges
rules.threshold: Check both association mechanisms
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on association absence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Service, its parent Business Service, incident volume, and any discovery or mapping evidence suggesting the CIs.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Application Service for an externally hosted or SaaS application.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 1 where mapping evidence supplies the CIs, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.title: CI supporting production service but tagged non-production
rules.whatItMeans: A CI tagged as non-production supports a production service.
rules.whyItMatters: Either the tag is wrong or a production service depends on non-production infrastructure. Both are serious, and which one it is changes who needs to know.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci.used_for, service used_for, svc_ci_assoc and cmdb_rel_ci
rules.detectionLogic: CIs with non-production used_for that support a service with production used_for
rules.threshold: Environment value sets configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — depends on environment tagging accuracy, which is itself CMDB-016.
rules.evidenceToShow: The CI, its environment tag, the production service, the supporting path, and the CI's discovery range environment.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Shared infrastructure legitimately serving both, with the tag reflecting primary use.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 — this is an architecture question, not a data fix

rules.title: Percentage of principal CIs reachable from a Business Capability
rules.whatItMeans: The percentage of principal-class CIs reachable by traversal from a Business Capability — the top of the CSDM model.
rules.whyItMatters: The full-chain reachability number. CMDB-057 measures reach from Business Service; this measures reach from the business layer above it, which is what determines whether business impact can be calculated at all.
rules.sourceTables: CSDM class hierarchy, cmdb_rel_ci, svc_ci_assoc
rules.detectionLogic: Traverse from every Business Capability downward; distinct principal CIs reached / total principal CIs
rules.threshold: Depth limit and threshold configurable; default threshold 40% Fallback (v3): when no principal classes are designated (see CMDB-139), evaluate all populated CMDB classes and name the fallback in the finding.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on traversal at the stated depth.
rules.evidenceToShow: Reachability percentage, the capability list, and the layer at which the chain most commonly breaks.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Estate not using Business Capability layer. Report scoped to the layers in use.

rules.title: CI associated to service with no relationship path
rules.whatItMeans: A CI is associated to a service via svc_ci_assoc but there is no relationship path between them in cmdb_rel_ci.
rules.whyItMatters: The association asserts a dependency the graph cannot substantiate. Consumers reading associations and consumers reading relationships get different answers.
rules.sourceTables: svc_ci_assoc, cmdb_rel_ci adjacency
rules.detectionLogic: Associations where no traversal path exists between the CI and the service within the depth limit
rules.threshold: Depth limit configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on path absence at stated depth.
rules.evidenceToShow: The association, the service, the CI, and the nearest partial path showing where the chain breaks.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Associations created deliberately to represent logical dependency with no physical path.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 1 where the missing edges are evidenced, Lane 3 otherwise
rules.crossDomainLink: Consistency between the two dependency mechanisms

rules.title: svc_ci_assoc and cmdb_rel_ci disagreeing
rules.whatItMeans: svc_ci_assoc and cmdb_rel_ci disagree: one asserts a service-CI link the other does not.
rules.whyItMatters: The two mechanisms have diverged. Which one a given feature reads determines the answer it gives, and the estate has two conflicting truths.
rules.sourceTables: svc_ci_assoc, cmdb_rel_ci filtered to service relationship types
rules.detectionLogic: Symmetric difference between the two link sets per service
rules.threshold: Report both directions of the difference separately
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on set comparison.
rules.evidenceToShow: Per service: links in associations only, links in relationships only, and links in both.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Estate deliberately uses one mechanism and populates the other partially.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 1 — reconcile toward the evidenced mechanism

rules.title: CI not associated to any Application Service
rules.whatItMeans: A CI is not associated to any Application Service.
rules.whyItMatters: The CI is outside the service model. It can be discovered, owned and healthy, and still never appear in a service impact result. Moderate rather than Critical because many CI classes legitimately sit outside the service layer.
rules.sourceTables: svc_ci_assoc, cmdb_rel_ci service edges, principal class list
rules.detectionLogic: Principal-class CIs with no association or edge to any Application Service
rules.threshold: Scope to classes expected to participate in the service model Fallback (v3): when no principal classes are designated (see CMDB-139), evaluate all populated CMDB classes and name the fallback in the finding.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on association absence.
rules.evidenceToShow: CI count by class, with the services their neighbours are associated to as a candidate signal.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Classes that legitimately sit outside the service model (network edge, facilities).
rules.remediationLane: Lane 1 where neighbours strongly indicate the service, Lane 3 otherwise

rules.title: CMDB Trust Score below threshold
rules.whatItMeans: The composite CMDB Trust Score — the weighted roll-up of completeness, correctness, uniqueness, identification, reconciliation, relationship integrity, freshness, ownership and consumption.
rules.whyItMatters: The single number for the executive view. Its value is entirely in being decomposable: every point lost traces to specific rules and specific records. Report raw, net of exceptions, and principal-class-only.
rules.sourceTables: All dimension scores D1-D10
rules.detectionLogic: Weighted sum with configurable weights; relationship integrity and uniqueness weighted highest
rules.threshold: Threshold configurable. Report the three variants always.
rules.confidenceBasis: Composite of the underlying dimension confidences. Decompose on demand.
rules.evidenceToShow: Full decomposition: dimension scores, contributing rules per dimension, record counts per rule.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Weights not reviewed by the customer — present the default-weight caveat.
rules.crossDomainLink: The headline; every other CMDB rule contributes

rules.title: Percentage of incidents referencing a Business Service
rules.whatItMeans: The percentage of incidents that reference a Business Service rather than a bare CI or nothing at all.
rules.whyItMatters: Measures whether the service model is actually used by the process that most needs it. Low values mean incidents cannot be aggregated by service, and service-level reporting is fiction.
rules.sourceTables: incident.business_service, incident volume
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(incidents with business_service populated) / COUNT(incidents) in the window
rules.threshold: Default threshold 60%. Window default 90 days.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ratio trend, distribution by assignment group, and the services that do get referenced for contrast.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Estate does not use service-based incident management by design.
rules.crossDomainLink: ITSM linkage; proves or disproves CMDB consumption

rules.title: Percentage of incidents referencing any CI
rules.whatItMeans: The percentage of incidents that reference any CI at all.
rules.whyItMatters: The most basic consumption measure. If incidents do not reference CIs, the CMDB is not part of the operational workflow regardless of how healthy it is.
rules.sourceTables: incident.cmdb_ci, incident volume
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(incidents with cmdb_ci populated) / COUNT(incidents) in the window
rules.threshold: Default threshold 50%
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ratio trend, distribution by category and group, and the classes most referenced.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Service-desk categories where CI reference is not meaningful (HR, facilities).

rules.title: Custom CI classes duplicating OOB class
rules.whatItMeans: Custom CI classes duplicate the function of an existing out-of-box class.
rules.whyItMatters: Splits the estate across two classes for the same thing. Identification rules, health rules and relationship rules apply to one and not the other, so half the population is ungoverned.
rules.sourceTables: Custom class definitions, attribute profiles, OOB class profiles
rules.detectionLogic: Custom classes whose attribute signature substantially overlaps an OOB class, with both populated
rules.threshold: Overlap threshold configurable; require both classes populated
rules.confidenceBasis: 85% — signature overlap is a strong but not conclusive indicator.
rules.evidenceToShow: Both classes, their attribute profiles, row counts, and the overlap percentage.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Custom class with a genuinely distinct purpose despite attribute overlap.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 — class consolidation is an architecture decision

rules.title: Class extension depth beyond recommended
rules.whatItMeans: CI class extension depth exceeds the recommended maximum.
rules.whyItMatters: Deep extension chains make attribute inheritance hard to reason about and slow class-based queries. A maintainability and performance signal rather than a correctness one.
rules.sourceTables: sys_db_object super_class chain within the CMDB tree
rules.detectionLogic: Classes whose extension depth from cmdb_ci exceeds threshold
rules.threshold: Default threshold 6 levels
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on depth arithmetic.
rules.evidenceToShow: Class hierarchy diagram with depth, row counts at each level, and the custom levels highlighted.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Deep OOB hierarchies that ServiceNow itself ships.

rules.title: CIs never referenced by any task in 12 months
rules.whatItMeans: CIs that have not been referenced by any task — incident, change, problem, request — in twelve months.
rules.whyItMatters: Either the CI is genuinely inert, or the processes are not using the CMDB. Both are worth knowing, and the distinction is made by comparing this against overall consumption rates.
rules.sourceTables: Task tables referencing cmdb_ci, CI list
rules.detectionLogic: CIs with zero task references in the window
rules.threshold: Window default 365 days
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on reference absence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Count by class, contrasted against the overall incident CI-reference rate to distinguish inert CIs from unused CMDB.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Infrastructure that legitimately never generates tickets.
rules.crossDomainLink: Retirement candidate population and consumption signal

rules.title: Classes with fewer than five records
rules.whatItMeans: CI classes containing fewer than five records.
rules.whyItMatters: Almost always a modelling mistake: a class created for a purpose that never materialised, or records that belong in a broader class. Adds governance surface with no benefit.
rules.sourceTables: Row counts per CMDB class
rules.detectionLogic: Classes with row count between 1 and 5
rules.threshold: Threshold configurable, default 5
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on count.
rules.evidenceToShow: Class list with row counts, creation dates, and the records themselves.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Genuinely rare CI types (a mainframe, a single specialised appliance).

rules.title: Custom attributes on OOB classes, unpopulated
rules.whatItMeans: Custom attributes added to out-of-box CI classes are unpopulated.
rules.whyItMatters: Someone added a field for a requirement that never completed. Adds schema weight, form clutter and upgrade surface with no data.
rules.sourceTables: sys_dictionary custom fields on OOB CMDB classes, population rates
rules.detectionLogic: Custom fields on OOB classes with population rate below threshold
rules.threshold: Default threshold 5% populated
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on population rate.
rules.evidenceToShow: Field list with class, population rate, creation date, and creating update set.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Fields for a programme not yet live.

rules.title: cmdb_rel_ci size ratio anomalous to CI count
rules.whatItMeans: The ratio of cmdb_rel_ci rows to cmdb_ci rows is anomalous — far above or far below the expected band for an estate of this shape.
rules.whyItMatters: A high ratio indicates duplicate edge generation, usually by a misconfigured integration or pattern. A low ratio indicates the graph is not being built at all. Both are diagnosable from one number.
rules.sourceTables: Row counts for cmdb_ci and cmdb_rel_ci, class composition
rules.detectionLogic: Relationship count / CI count, compared to the expected band derived from class composition
rules.threshold: Expected band derived from class mix, not a fixed number. State the derivation.
rules.confidenceBasis: Confidence depends on the expected-band derivation. Report the band and the derivation.
rules.evidenceToShow: The ratio, the expected band, the derivation, and the classes contributing most to the anomaly.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Unusual but legitimate estate shape (heavily network-weighted estates run higher).
rules.remediationLane: Lane 2 where an integration is generating duplicate edges

rules.title: Class growing with no corresponding discovery activity
rules.whatItMeans: A CI class is growing in row count with no corresponding discovery activity.
rules.whyItMatters: Something other than discovery is creating CIs in a class discovery is supposed to own. Usually an integration bypassing IRE, which is CMDB-046 seen from the growth side.
rules.sourceTables: Class row counts over snapshots, discovery_device_history, CI creation attribution
rules.detectionLogic: Classes with positive growth AND no corresponding discovery creation volume in the window
rules.threshold: Requires at least 2 snapshots
rules.confidenceBasis: 95% — depends on creation attribution accuracy.
rules.evidenceToShow: Growth chart, creation source breakdown, and the specific integration or script responsible.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Legitimate non-discovery source for that class (cloud API, CMDB feed).

rules.title: Slow transactions on CI tables
rules.whatItMeans: Slow transactions are attributable to queries against CI tables.
rules.whyItMatters: Connects CMDB scale to user-visible performance. Gives the platform team a reason to care about CMDB size that is not abstract.
rules.sourceTables: syslog_transaction aggregated by URL and table, CI table row counts
rules.detectionLogic: Transactions above the slow threshold whose primary table is a CMDB table, ranked by total time
rules.threshold: Slow threshold configurable, default 95th percentile
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on attribution where transaction data identifies the table.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ranked transaction list with table, average and total time, frequency, and the responsible list, report or script.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: One-off bulk operations during a migration window.

rules.title: Large classes without appropriate indexing
rules.whatItMeans: Large CI classes lack indexes supporting the queries actually run against them.
rules.whyItMatters: The specific, fixable cause behind most of CMDB-126. An index on the right column is a Lane 2 update set and often a dramatic improvement.
rules.sourceTables: Table row counts, index definitions, query patterns from transaction data
rules.detectionLogic: Large tables where high-frequency query predicates have no supporting index
rules.threshold: Size threshold configurable; query frequency from the observation window
rules.confidenceBasis: 90% — index recommendations depend on query pattern sampling.
rules.evidenceToShow: Table, row count, the frequent query predicates, existing indexes, and the proposed index.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Index deliberately omitted due to write-cost concerns.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 2 — index creation via update set, tested first

rules.title: Relationship table growth rate
rules.whatItMeans: The growth rate of the relationship table over time.
rules.whyItMatters: Trend measure feeding CMDB-124. A growth rate diverging from CI growth is the early signal of edge duplication.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_rel_ci row counts over snapshots
rules.detectionLogic: Rows added per period, trended, alongside CI growth for comparison
rules.threshold: Requires at least 3 snapshots for a meaningful trend
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on counts. Trend confidence from window length.
rules.evidenceToShow: Growth chart for relationships and CIs side by side, with the ratio trend.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Active service mapping rollout legitimately adding edges.

rules.title: Row count and growth per class
rules.whatItMeans: Row count and growth rate per CI class.
rules.whyItMatters: Baseline measure rather than a defect. Feeds class prioritisation, archival policy and several other rules. Report it because everything else references it.
rules.sourceTables: Aggregate API counts per class over snapshots
rules.detectionLogic: Row count and period-over-period growth per class
rules.threshold: Report as a table, ranked by growth
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on counts.
rules.evidenceToShow: Ranked class table with count, growth rate, and projected size.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: None — this is a measure.

rules.title: Rotation/archival not configured on CMDB history tables
rules.whatItMeans: Table rotation or archival is not configured on CMDB history and audit tables.
rules.whyItMatters: These tables grow faster than the CMDB itself and are rarely queried. Unbounded growth with no retention mechanism is both a performance and a compliance issue.
rules.sourceTables: Table rotation configuration, sys_audit and history table sizes
rules.detectionLogic: CMDB-related history and audit tables with no rotation or archival configured
rules.threshold: Table list configurable
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on configuration absence.
rules.evidenceToShow: Table list with current size, growth rate, and rotation config state.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Rotation handled at the instance level.

rules.title: Net position negative (creating faster than resolving)
rules.whatItMeans: Net position: defects resolved versus defects created over the period.
rules.whyItMatters: The only number that says whether the estate is getting better. A team can remediate ten thousand findings and still be losing. This is the metric that justifies the governance subscription over the one-time assessment.
rules.sourceTables: Finding sets across successive assessment snapshots
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(findings closed in period) MINUS COUNT(findings created in period), by domain and overall
rules.threshold: Requires at least 2 snapshots. Report by domain.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the arithmetic, subject to consistent rule versions across snapshots. State rule version.
rules.evidenceToShow: Net position chart by domain, with created and closed counts shown separately.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Rule pack version changed between snapshots, making counts non-comparable. Always compare like rule versions.

rules.title: Previously remediated findings reappearing
rules.whatItMeans: Findings that were previously remediated have reappeared.
rules.whyItMatters: Proof that the fix did not hold, which is almost always because the prevention control was never implemented. Every regression is an argument for the companion prevention finding that should have accompanied the original fix.
rules.sourceTables: Finding history across snapshots, remediation records
rules.detectionLogic: Findings matching a previously closed finding on rule and object, recreated after closure
rules.threshold: Match on rule ID plus object identity
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on match. Cause attribution to a missing prevention control at 90%.
rules.evidenceToShow: The original finding, its remediation record and date, the regression, and whether a prevention control was implemented.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Object legitimately changed again for a valid reason.
rules.crossDomainLink: Justifies prevention findings and continuous governance

rules.title: Rate of IRE bypass rising
rules.whatItMeans: The rate at which CI creates bypass IRE is increasing.
rules.whyItMatters: The trend view of CMDB-046. A rising bypass rate means duplicate creation will accelerate regardless of how many duplicates are currently being cleaned up.
rules.sourceTables: IRE bypass ratio across snapshots
rules.detectionLogic: CMDB-046 ratio trended across snapshots
rules.threshold: Flag on sustained positive trend above noise
rules.confidenceBasis: Trend confidence from snapshot count and variance.
rules.evidenceToShow: Bypass rate trend chart with attribution to specific integrations over time.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: One-time migration inflating a single period.

rules.title: New duplicates since last assessment
rules.whatItMeans: Duplicate sets created since the previous assessment.
rules.whyItMatters: Distinguishes the backlog from the inflow. Cleaning the backlog while the inflow continues is the most common wasted effort in CMDB remediation.
rules.sourceTables: Duplicate set membership across snapshots
rules.detectionLogic: Duplicate sets present in the current snapshot and absent from the previous
rules.threshold: Requires 2 snapshots with comparable rule versions
rules.confidenceBasis: Inherits duplicate detection confidence.
rules.evidenceToShow: New duplicate count, attribution by creating source, and comparison against the remediated count.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Rule threshold changed between snapshots.

rules.title: Newly stale CI count per week
rules.whatItMeans: The count of CIs newly becoming stale each week.
rules.whyItMatters: Leading indicator. A rising newly-stale rate means a discovery source is degrading now, before the accumulated staleness becomes visible in the overall score.
rules.sourceTables: last_discovered distribution across snapshots
rules.detectionLogic: CIs crossing the staleness threshold per week, by class and by discovery range
rules.threshold: Staleness threshold per class
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on arithmetic.
rules.evidenceToShow: Weekly newly-stale count by range and class, with the discovery schedule and its recent run history for each.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Schedule interval changed, shifting the threshold.
rules.crossDomainLink: Earliest warning of an ITOM failure

rules.title: Relationship count trend declining
rules.whatItMeans: The relationship count trend is declining across snapshots.
rules.whyItMatters: The slow-motion version of CMDB-056. A gradual decline is harder to notice than a collapse and just as damaging over a year.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_rel_ci counts by class across snapshots
rules.detectionLogic: Negative trend in relationship count per class across snapshots
rules.threshold: Requires at least 3 snapshots
rules.confidenceBasis: Trend confidence from window length and variance.
rules.evidenceToShow: Trend chart by class, with deletion attribution from audit.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Planned decommissioning programme.

rules.title: Health score trend declining
rules.whatItMeans: The overall health score trend is declining.
rules.whyItMatters: The summary trend. Its value is in attribution: which dimensions and which rules drove the decline, not the number itself.
rules.sourceTables: Composite score across snapshots
rules.detectionLogic: Score trend with per-dimension attribution of the change
rules.threshold: Requires comparable rule versions across snapshots
rules.confidenceBasis: Inherits composite confidence. State rule version comparability.
rules.evidenceToShow: Score trend with a waterfall showing which dimensions contributed to the movement.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Rule pack version change. Never compare scores across rule versions without saying so.

rules.title: Attestation adherence trend
rules.whatItMeans: The trend in attestation completion adherence over successive cycles.
rules.whyItMatters: Governance adherence over time. Declining adherence predicts declining data quality with a lag, and it is the earliest evidence that a governance programme is losing support.
rules.sourceTables: Attestation completion rates per cycle
rules.detectionLogic: Completion rate per cycle, trended
rules.threshold: Requires at least 3 cycles
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on completion rates. Trend confidence from cycle count.
rules.evidenceToShow: Adherence trend by cycle, with breakdown by attester and class.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Cycle scope changed between periods.

rules.title: No principal classes designated
rules.whatItMeans: No CMDB class is flagged principal in cmdb_class_info, so nothing distinguishes the classes that carry operational weight from peripheral ones.
rules.whyItMatters: Every principal-scoped rule (CMDB-004, 005, 006, 014, 017, 019, 045, 057, 058, 085, 091, 104, 112, 115) has no defined population and must fall back to every populated class, so a core router is weighed the same as a meeting-room printer.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_class_info.principal_class
rules.detectionLogic: COUNT(cmdb_class_info WHERE principal_class=true) = 0, on a complete read of cmdb_class_info
rules.threshold: Fixed: zero principal classes. Escalate to Systemic when the fallback population (all populated classes) includes classes whose CIs support a Business Critical service. While it fires, every dimension with principal-scoped rules carries a coverage caveat.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% — structural absence on a complete read.
rules.evidenceToShow: cmdb_class_info row count, principal count of zero, and the populated classes (with CI counts) used as the fallback population.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: cmdb_class_info rows hidden by ACL — the read must be complete; a version where the principal flag is recorded elsewhere — confirm the field exists before raising.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 — guided decision (choosing principal classes is a CMDB owner's judgement)
rules.crossDomainLink: Defines the population for every principal-scoped rule in Groups 1–11

rules.title: Identity attributes missing on classes whose identification rule uses them
rules.whatItMeans: A CI's identification rule can only match it on attributes that are populated. When every strong entry of that rule (serial, product instance id, MAC — anything other than name) is unsatisfiable for the CI, IRE can recognise it only by name, or not at all.
rules.whyItMatters: The next discovery or integration payload for that device either creates a second CI or merges on name alone. This is the completeness-side cause of Group 4 duplicates, and the record-level mirror of CMDB-044 (rules that are name-only by design).
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_identifier (applies_to, active); cmdb_identifier_entry (identifier, table, attributes, order, allow_null_attribute, active); the CI's own attributes; lookup tables an entry names (cmdb_serial_number.cmdb_ci, cmdb_ci_network_adapter.cmdb_ci).
rules.detectionLogic: For each CI: take the nearest active identifier in its class lineage. For each active entry whose attributes include a non-descriptive attribute, the entry is satisfiable when (entry.table is in the CI's lineage AND every attribute is populated and not a placeholder, unless allow_null_attribute) OR (entry.table is a lookup table AND a row references the CI). Flag CIs where no strong entry is satisfiable.
rules.threshold: Descriptive attributes default: name. Placeholder set as CMDB-017. Configurable. Scoped by identifier usage, not by hardware or network class.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on attribute emptiness for own-table entries. Lookup-table entries are satisfied by the existence of a referencing row; a lookup read that fails leaves the CI unflagged rather than guessed.
rules.evidenceToShow: The CI, its identification rule, each strong entry with the empty attribute(s) or missing lookup row, and the weak entry (name) it would fall back to.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: CIs identified through a lookup table the rule names (serial number table, network adapters) — checked before flagging. Dependent identifiers (hosted/contained CIs) identify through their parent.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 then Lane 1 — source the identity attribute from discovery or asset, then bulk apply
rules.crossDomainLink: Completeness-side cause of Group 4 duplicates (CMDB-033 to 041); mirror of CMDB-044

rules.title: Impact analysis returning no affected services
rules.whatItMeans: When a change or an alert names a CI, ServiceNow calculates which services it affects. This measures how often that calculation comes back non-empty.
rules.whyItMatters: The single honest measure of whether the CMDB works. When it is empty, change risk, alert prioritisation and outage impact are all computed as nothing affected — the router scenario as one number: the alert was right, the CI was right, the answer was empty.
rules.sourceTables: change_request (cmdb_ci); task_cmdb_ci_service (task, cmdb_ci_service) — a change's impacted services; em_alert (cmdb_ci) and Event Management's impacted-service records for alerts (table name to confirm on an ITOM-activated instance).
rules.detectionLogic: KPI = COUNT(service-bound changes with at least one task_cmdb_ci_service row) / COUNT(service-bound changes), over the ITSM slice (open, or updated in the last 90 days); alerts the same way where Event Management is active. A change is service-bound when its CI should resolve to a service: it is associated in svc_ci_assoc, reachable downward from a service in cmdb_rel_ci, or is itself a service with business criticality set. Standalone CIs are not counted against the rate. Finding when the KPI is below threshold.
rules.threshold: Default 90% (confirmed 17 Sep — configurable). Percentage rule: a D10 KPI sub-score; gates when below threshold (systemic_kind measured_kpi).
rules.confidenceBasis: Computed ratio over the records read, with the denominator stated. An empty impacted-services list cannot distinguish calculated-and-found-nothing from never-calculated, so the guard applies.
rules.evidenceToShow: The ratio with numerator and denominator, a sample of changes with a CI and no impacted service, and the status of the alert half.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: Impacted-service calculation disabled or never triggered for changes (the refresh is manual or turned off) — confirm it runs before treating an empty result as a CMDB defect.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 — guided decision; the fix is the service model and relationships (D6, Group 11), not this measure
rules.crossDomainLink: Caused by D6 relationship gaps, CSDM linkage (Group 11) and event binding (ITOM); causes ITSM change-risk and Event Management impact failures. Surfaced in the gate narrative.

rules.title: Mass write presented as freshness
rules.whatItMeans: A large share of CIs carry the same sys_updated_on from the same writer, with nothing to show that the write changed any attribute. The records look recently maintained; the touch carries no information about whether what they say is still true.
rules.whyItMatters: Every record-level freshness measure reads a bulk write as maintenance. One synchronised job makes a whole estate look cared for and hides those records from the rules that would otherwise find them — permanently, because the timestamp never gets older than the job. It is the inverse of a stale record: touched, but the touch means nothing. This rule exists to stop that population disappearing.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci.sys_updated_on, sys_updated_by, sys_mod_count; sys_audit (opt-in) for the attribute-level deltas that separate a migration from a no-op.
rules.detectionLogic: Group in-scope CIs by (date of sys_updated_on, sys_updated_by). A group covering at least the configured share of in-scope CIs is a bulk touch, and every CI in it is charged. Where sys_audit is read, a group whose CIs show real field changes on that date is a legitimate migration and is exempt; where it is not read, the migration test is declared unverified and confidence is reduced.
rules.threshold: Default share 20% of in-scope CIs, on one day, from one writer. Configurable.
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the timestamp clustering itself. Whether the write carried attribute changes is verifiable only where sys_audit is read; otherwise the rule states the test as unverified and drops to 0.8.
rules.evidenceToShow: The date, the writer, the CI count, the share of the estate, and whether attribute deltas could be checked at all.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: A genuine bulk migration or reclassification DOES change attributes. Read sys_audit (opt-in) before acting, and exempt the writer if the deltas are real.
rules.remediationLane: Lane 3 — bring the population under a source that confirms it, rather than a job that touches it
rules.crossDomainLink: Suppresses CMDB-075 and every record-level freshness signal; the population CMDB-076 would have caught if attribute metadata existed

rules.title: Percentage of CIs whose most recent write is a bulk touch
rules.whatItMeans: The share of in-scope CIs whose latest write belongs to a synchronised mass touch rather than to anything that confirmed the record.
rules.whyItMatters: It is the one number that says whether this CMDB's freshness can be believed at all. Above the threshold, every age-based measure in the model is reporting the schedule of a job rather than the state of the estate, so the composite's freshness component means nothing — which is what gating is for.
rules.sourceTables: cmdb_ci.sys_updated_on, sys_updated_by; the bulk-touch groups derived by CMDB-142.
rules.detectionLogic: KPI = COUNT(in-scope CIs whose latest write is NOT part of a bulk-touch group) / COUNT(in-scope CIs). Published as the passing half so that higher is better. Finding when the bulk-touch share exceeds the threshold.
rules.threshold: Default ceiling 25% of in-scope CIs. Percentage rule: a D7 KPI sub-score; gates when breached (systemic_kind measured_kpi).
rules.confidenceBasis: 100% on the ratio, over the CIs read. Shares the migration caveat of CMDB-142.
rules.evidenceToShow: The ratio with numerator and denominator, the contributing bulk-touch groups with their dates and writers, and whether attribute deltas were checkable.
rules.falsePositiveGuard: An estate mid-migration will breach this legitimately and briefly. Check whether the writes carry attribute deltas, and whether the share falls on the next run.
rules.crossDomainLink: The measured form of CMDB-142; contrast with CMDB-076 attribute freshness
